correctness.rationale: PASS for the precise FINITE capped statement. Starting from gamma=(0,2,4,7,3,8,6,1,5), with each cyclic position rotation identified and Vernitski's exact T±, X, R, S definitions, I reconstructed both the package BFS and an independent two-stage exhaustive closure calculation. D_9(gamma) has 18 words; all admissible additions from these yield 2916 distinct eleven-petal seeds. Closing those under R and S gives precisely 3168 eleven-petal words; their 144 distinct D_11 orbits each have size 22, so all stabilizers are trivial. An independent complete test of every crossing-exchange basepoint and height pair found zero applicable X across all 3186 states. All eleven-petal deletions land in the nine-petal gamma orbit, nine-petal states have no deletion/X, and every eleven-petal orbit contains a directly added seed. Thus the enumerated union is closed under every allowed capped move, contains gamma and is entirely reachable, and its simple quotient is K_{1,144}; all inter-orbit edges are T±. The independent 2-stage algorithm did not use the source's BFS for completeness. The known 3186/18/3168 totals from Vernitski independently cross-check. The package script, inspected before execution and transcribed for a local replay, also prints VERIFY_OK with the same orbit and edge profile. No claim is made about paths with at least 13 petals or the unrestricted move graph. The Git source tree was independently reconstructed by Git tree-object SHA-1 from all seven actual returned entries and matched the assigned SHA; locally transcribed script bytes differ from the repository blob and are not claimed to be identical.

Hence no stronger covering implication was identified.

value.rationale: PASS: The object is not an arbitrary subcase but the exact finite component that certifies the first published excess-four nine-petal hard unknot gamma. Its natural dihedral quotient collapses a 3186-vertex trapped move graph to 145 vertices and classifies every eleven-petal symmetry type as a free D_11 orbit attached to one nine-petal type. The new zero-X property explains why the quotient has no lateral transitions, rather than merely restating the known total 3168. This naturally motivated complete classification is a reusable structural benchmark for later petal-move/quotient studies; no broad theorem or conjectural impact is asserted. It is finite and derivative of a known enumeration, but the orbit graph is not mechanically forced by the published aggregate counts.
